Data-driven robust optimization scheduling for microgrid day-ahead to
intra-day operations based on renewable energy interval prediction
Mao Yang , Jinxin Wang
*
, Yiming Chen , Yuxuan Zeng , Xin Su
Key Laboratory of Modern Power System Simulation and Control & Renewable Energy Technology, Ministry of Education (Northeast Electric Power University), Jilin,
132012, China
ARTICLE INFO
Keywords:
Microgrid
Renewable energy interval prediction
GPR
Robust optimization
MDQN
ABSTRACT
The uncertainty in renewable energy forecasting significantly impacts microgrid scheduling, and traditional
scheduling schemes are often overly conservative and limited by a single time scale, resulting in unreasonable
strategies that fail to balance reliability and cost-effectiveness. Based on this, a comprehensive two-stage day-
ahead and intra-day microgrid scheduling framework is proposed integrating forecasting, regulation, and
decision-making. Based on historical power data of renewable energy, a multi-kernel covariance function is
applied to improve Gaussian process regression (GPR) for adaptively generating renewable energy power pre-
diction intervals at various confidence levels and verifies the construction of robust optimization uncertainty
scenario sets. In the day-ahead scheduling phase, a two-stage adaptive robust optimization model based on in-
terval probability uncertainty sets is established to ensure minimal scheduling costs under the worst-case sce-
nario. Meanwhile, a modified deep Q network (MDQN) algorithm based on a k-priority sampling strategy is
proposed to transform the two-stage iterative process into a discrete Markov decision process for solution. In the
intra-day scheduling phase, the day-ahead scheduling scheme is followed, and the intra-day scheduling scheme is
optimized through multi-time-scale rolling optimization to reduce the impact of renewable energy power fluc-
tuations. Case studies validate that the proposed scheduling method ensures robustness against uncertainties in
renewable energy output while also maintaining the economic efficiency of system operations.
1. Introduction
Microgrid, as effective forms of integrating various types of distrib-
uted generation, are considered as viable solutions to the challenges
posed by the large-scale integration of renewable energy [ 1 , 2 ]. How-
ever, the output of renewable energy is characterized by randomness
and volatility, which pose significant challenges to the safe and eco-
nomic scheduling of microgrid. Therefore, it is crucial to explore how to
maximize the utilization of renewable energy while ensuring the safe
and economical operation of the system, highlighting the substantial
research value and significance of this topic [ 3 , 4 ].
Currently, the main approaches to addressing the uncertainty of
renewable energy output in microgrid include spinning reserve capacity
[ 5 ], stochastic programming [ 6 , 7 ], and robust optimization [ 8 , 9 ]. The
main advantage of spinning reserve capacity is its simplicity and effec-
tiveness. While the standby capacity is sufficiently large, it can effec-
tively address uncertainties in the system. However, maintaining
standby status for reserve units increases the system ’ s investment costs,
and any unused standby capacity leads to resource wastage, making it
economically unviable [ 10 ]. Stochastic programming directly uses the
probability distributions of random variables, enabling a more accurate
depiction of system uncertainties. However, its technical challenge lies
in the difficulty of precisely describing the probability distributions of
uncertain parameters and scenarios occurrences [ 11 ]. Furthermore, as
the number of scenarios increases, the complexity of solving the models
also rises. The approach of reducing scenarios, which simplifies uncer-
tain variables from their original interval domain to a number of
representative scenarios for multi-scenario deterministic optimization,
risks losing the traversability of the uncertainty interval, making it
difficult to ensure robustness. Moreover, if the clustering algorithm lacks
precision, the resulting “ typical ” scenarios may not possess sufficient
representation [ 12 ]. Robust optimization, as a powerful tool for
addressing uncertainty in stochastic optimization problems, has the
advantage of not requiring prior knowledge of the probability distri-
bution of uncertain variables. By describing variable uncertainties in the
form of sets, it ensures that constraints are satisfied for all possible

values within a known set of uncertain variables. Due to its low re-
quirements for describing uncertain variables, robust optimization has
attracted considerable attention in microgrid energy management [13].
The core technique of robust optimization lies in the selection of
uncertainty variable sets. He et al. [14] uses box uncertainty variable
sets to describe the uncertainty of source-load output, considering the
source-load output as fluctuating within a defined interval without
considering its specific probability distribution. Qin et al. [15] combines
box uncertainty sets with two-stage robust optimization to construct a
two-stage robust optimization scheduling model with a min-max-min
structure. Yan et al. [16] considers multiple uncertainties in the sys-
tem, integrating a stochastic hierarchical scenario generation method
with a box uncertainty set to address multi-objective optimization and
multi-stage coupling problems. In the above references, the construction
of the box uncertainty set inadequately considers the adjustment of set
conservatism, resulting in limitations in capturing the diversity and
dynamic changes of uncertain variables. Consequently, the flexibility of
scheduling is constrained, and the decision-making tend to be overly
conservative.
To address this drawback, Shi et al. [17] introduces uncertainty
constraints into the model to generate polyhedral uncertain sets, thereby
adjusting the conservatism of robust optimization results. Wu et al. [18]
considers the uncertainties of new energy output and uncoordinated
charging of electric vehicles, constructing a robust optimization model
with polyhedral uncertainty sets. By capturing the worst-case scenarios
under different conditions, the model ensures the system’s stable and
efficient operation under various unexpected situations. In Ref. [19], a
day-ahead to intra-day optimal scheduling framework based on robust
optimization and stochastic optimization methods is proposed,
employing a polyhedral uncertainty set to represent the uncertainties in
wind power and load. Yuan et al. [20] considers the correlations be-
tween uncertain variables, employing elliptical uncertainty sets to
obtain the wind power time correlation axis and centre point, forming a
wind power time correlation polyhedral uncertainty sets. The above
studies have improved scheduling flexibility by adjusting the uncer-
tainty of uncertain variables and have reduced the conservativeness of
robust optimization to some extent. However, issues remain regarding
the overly coarse of uncertain variables and subjectively predetermined
target deviation factors. Additionally, insufficient consideration is given
to the historical data and distribution information of uncertain vari-
ables, which actually disconnects the relationship between prediction
and scheduling.
Currently, some scholars have proposed a robust optimization
method that uses data-driven representations of system uncertainty sets.
Zhang et al. [21] constructs an uncertain set using historical data that
combines wind power output and traffic flow, proposing a data-driven
two-stage robust scheduling model. Ye et al. [22] develops a wind
power uncertain set based on a “closed-loop feedback” data-driven
approach and presents a robust scheduling method that accounts for
the uncertainty set of historical wind power prediction errors. Refer-
ences [21,22] considers prediction data with varying accuracy during
the forecasting stage but insufficiently explores the inherent features of
historical data, resulting in suboptimal economic efficiency and
robustness of the scheduling scheme in certain extreme scenarios. Ref-
erences [23,24] employs a minimum volume enclosing convex hull
uncertainty set, considering the spatiotemporal correlations of wind
power, and proposes a data-driven robust optimization model for
coordinating the scheduling of multi-energy coupling systems. Zhao
et al. [25] uses generative adversarial networks to generate artificial
wind power data to improve the estimation of worst-case probability
distributions in robust optimization, thereby adjusting the robustness of
the optimization solution in terms of cost-effectiveness. The above
research models uncertainty through historical data or prediction errors
and estimates their distribution using statistical methods. However, it
lacks sufficient feature extraction from the historical data and does not
incorporate the characteristics contained in the prediction data. Base on
this, references [26,27] constructs a Wasserstein fuzzy set using histor-
ical sample data, which accurately captures the prediction errors of
source-load output. However, the representational effectiveness of the
Wasserstein fuzzy set largely depends on the selected fuzziness param-
eter and probability level. Inappropriate parameter settings may result
in overly conservative scheduling outcomes or inadequate robustness.
Additionally, under extreme conditions, the Wasserstein fuzzy set may
fail to fully capture actual dynamic changes, potentially limiting the
model’s ability to effectively address the system’s real risks.
Currently, solutions for robust optimization models commonly
employ traditional intelligent algorithms or mathematical methods
based on robust optimization. Dong et al. [28] proposes a constrained
multi-objective transfer algorithm to solve multi-objective optimization
problems with the operational costs and robustness of integrated energy
systems as optimization goals. Although this method can balance mul-
tiple optimization objectives, it has poor convergence and often fails to
find the optimal value when dealing with programming problems
involving complex constraints. Luan et al. [29] proposes a robust
improved particle swarm optimization algorithm, which dynamically
determines the optimal solution using the longest distance expectation
fitness evaluation strategy in an n-dimensional space. However, due to
the high complexity of the algorithm, it can lead to long computation
times when handling high-dimensional problems. Shen et al. [30] em-
ploys a column constraint generation algorithm to solve a robust opti-
mization model considering renewable energy uncertainty and carbon
emissions. However, as the size of the problem increases, the complexity
of the model prevents the algorithm from consistently maintaining an
optimal solution. Cai et al. [31] uses a distributed algorithm based on
the bisection method combined with a column constraint generation
algorithm to address the low-level non-convex planning convergence
difficulties in two-stage robust optimization models. However, it still
faces poor convergence and long computation times when handling
complex non-convex problems. Therefore, traditional intelligent algo-
rithms often require a long time for optimization due to cross-iteration
and are prone to getting trapped in local extrema. Furthermore,
mathematically-based robust optimization methods necessitate the
establishment of complex mathematical models, which are less appli-
cable in scenarios with high-dimensional optimization variables.
In addition, the scheduling model constructed in the above studies
are concentrated on the day-ahead time horizon. However, as the pre-
dictive time-scale shortens, the forecast accuracy of new energy power
and load demand improves, thus the day-ahead scheduling plans cannot
be directly adopted in the intra-day scheduling. A proper adjustment of
the scheduling plans based on more accurate intra-day prediction data is
essential. Therefore, it is necessary to study multi-time scale optimiza-
tion strategies to adapt to different uncertainties caused by prediction
accuracy variations. References [32,33] proposed multi-time scale
optimization strategies based on the multi-energy flexibility. References
[34,35] constructed stochastic optimization and robust optimization
models to address uncertainties in new energy output and load demand
during day-ahead to intra-day scheduling. However, the consideration
of uncertainties in the above studies at the day-ahead stage tends to be
overly risky or conservative: the former results in excessive costs for
intra-day tracking of the day-ahead plan, sometimes failing to fully
mitigate power fluctuations, while the latter may lead to total costs
exceeding acceptable levels.
To address the above problems, this paper proposes a two-stage day-
ahead and intra-day microgrid scheduling framework integrating fore-
casting, regulation, and decision-making. The main innovations are as
follows.
1) Based on historical power data of wind and photovoltaic and com-
bined with the covered probabilistic information, a multi-kernel
covariance function is used to improve the GPR algorithm for
adaptive generation of prediction intervals. Chance constraints are
introduced to combine probabilistic confidence intervals with robust

2) In the day-ahead scheduling phase, a two-stage adaptive robust

established to ensure minimal scheduling costs of microgrid under
the worst-case scenario. In the intra-day scheduling phase, the day-
ahead scheduling scheme is followed, and the intra-day scheduling

reduce the impact of renewable energy power fluctuations.
3) To address the issues of high modelling complexity and low solution
efficiency in traditional methods, a k-prioritized sampling strategy is
introduced into the DQN algorithm, constructing a MDQN algorithm
that transforms the two-stage iterative process into a discrete Markov
decision process. The proposed method is validated to effectively
reduce model complexity and improve solution efficiency while
ensuring the robustness of economic scheduling in microgrid.

2.3. Algorithm implementation steps and workflow
To effectively handle the multimodal and uncertainty features of
historical data of renewable energy, this paper employs the fuzzy C-

3. The robust optimization dispatch of microgrids for day-ahead
and intra-day based on interval prediction of renewable energy
The microgrid structure is shown in Fig. 2 , including wind turbine
(WT), photovoltaic (PV), micro-gas turbine (MT), fuel cell (FC), energy
storage system (ESS), and load.
To reduce power fluctuations caused by deviations in renewable
energy forecasts for both day-ahead and intra-day periods, a two-stage
robust optimization scheduling model for microgrid is established. The
model framework is showed in Fig. 3 and representation of rolling
optimization process is showed in Fig. 4 . The day-ahead scheduling is
divided into pre-scheduling and re-scheduling phases. The pre-
scheduling phase aims to minimize the startup and shutdown costs of
MT and FC by formulating a startup and shutdown plan to address any
scenario of concentrated uncertainty. The re-scheduling phase focuses
on minimizing the daily generation costs of the microgrid, formulating
optimal scheduling plan that ensures minimal day-ahead scheduling
costs under the worst-case scenario. The intra-day rolling scheduling
follows the day-ahead plan, smoothing power fluctuations of renewable
energy through multi-time scale rolling optimization of 1 h and 15 min.
The long-term intra-day rolling adjusts MT, FC, and purchased power
from the power grid to smooth renewable energy fluctuations, while the
short-term rolling adjusts energy storage power and load curtailment to
address rapid fluctuations in renewable energy output. At the beginning
of each rolling cycle during the intra-day, the forecast values within the
prediction horizon are updated, and the output plan within the opti-
mization control horizon is optimized. However, only the planned re-
sults for the first time period are issued.

6. Conclusions
This paper proposes a robust optimization scheduling method for
day-ahead and intra-day microgrid that integrates prediction, adjust-
ment, and decision-making. The method uses an improved GPR algo-
rithm to adaptively generate the interval prediction of renewable energy
output under different confidence levels, linking it to the construction of
the robust optimization uncertainty set. A MDQN algorithm is intro-
duced to transform the robust model into a discrete Markov decision
process for solution. Through case analysis, the following conclusions
are drawn.
1) By comparing the interval prediction performance of different pre-
diction models, it is verified that the proposed FCMCA-RQ&Ma-GPR
prediction method can focus more uncertainty information within
narrower interval boundaries. The constructed uncertainty set has a
stronger overall probability coverage ability at the same confidence
level, proving the effectiveness of the proposed prediction model.
2) The proposed adaptive robust optimization method based on interval
probability uncertainty sets is compared with adaptive robust opti-
mization methods using μ type uncertainty sets, Γ type uncertainty
sets, and Dirichlet process-generated uncertainty sets. The results
show that the proposed method has the lowest operating cost for the
microgrid at different confidence levels. The scheduling plan
formulated by this method better copes with the uncertainty of
renewable energy output, reducing the conservatism of scheduling
decisions while ensuring the economic efficiency and robustness of
system operation.
3) By comparing the proposed MDQN algorithm with the DQN algo-
rithm, C&CG algorithm, and GA, it is shown that the proposed al-
gorithm can effectively reduce model complexity and improve
solving efficiency while ensuring the optimal cost function value of
the objective function, demonstrating the superior solving perfor-
mance of the MDQN algorithm.
The application premise of the proposed adaptive robust optimiza-
tion model based on interval probability uncertainty sets requires a large
amount of historical new energy power data. Insufficient data may lead
to inadequate mining of the probability information and characteristics
contained in the historical new energy power data. Additionally, this
paper’s exploration of extreme weather scenarios remains insufficient,
which may result in the final decision being overly “risky.” Next,
extreme weather scenarios will be considered, and incremental learning
algorithms will be used to characterize system uncertainty, applying
them to the robust optimization model to further improve the accuracy
of microgrid scheduling decisions under uncertainty, avoiding overly
“conservative” or “risky” decisions to the greatest extent possible.
